questions.skill: Compare properties of two functions represented in different ways
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: f(x) = 3x + 2. The table shows g. Which function has the greater value at x = 3? Which has the greater average rate of change from x = 0 to x = 3?
questions.prompt_markup:
f(x) = 3x + 2. The table shows g.
Which function has the greater value at x = 3? Which has the greater average rate of change from x = 0 to x = 3?
questions.correct_answer: g at x = 3 (16 compared with 11); g has the greater rate (5 compared with 3).
questions.grading_note: Form required: both comparisons with values.

questions.prompt_markup:
Function f has y-intercept 4 and increases by 5 for each 1-unit increase in x. g(x) = 5x - 1.

questions.correct_answer: Same slope, 5; f has the greater y-intercept (4 compared with -1), so their graphs are parallel lines.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both comparisons.

questions.skill: Compare periodic functions given in different forms
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: f(x) = 3sin(2x). Function g has amplitude 4 and period π. Which has the greater amplitude? Do they have the same period?
questions.prompt_markup:
f(x) = 3sin(2x). Function g has amplitude 4 and period π.
Which has the greater amplitude? Do they have the same period?
questions.correct_answer: g has the greater amplitude (4 compared with 3); yes, both periods are π.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both parts. The period of f is 2π ÷ 2.

questions.prompt_markup:
Tide A rises to 12 ft and falls to 2 ft. Tide B is h(t) = 6 + 4sin t.
Which has the greater amplitude?
questions.correct_answer: Tide A: 5 ft compared with 4 ft.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the tide and both amplitudes. (12 - 2) ÷ 2 = 5.
